## Housing Crisis Deepens

South Korea's rental market is experiencing unprecedented strain, particularly among young people struggling with soaring monthly costs. New data reveals that small officetel units under 30 square meters commanding over 1 million won monthly rent have surged sixfold over the past five years. In Seoul's university districts, students are paying up to 1.2 million won monthly for just 5-pyeong units, placing severe pressure on household budgets for the nation's youth population. The proportion of officetel contracts above 1 million won now accounts for one in eight transactions across Seoul, underscoring a fundamental shift in the rental landscape that demands urgent policy intervention.

## Government Housing Intervention Strategy

Deputy Prime Minister Lee Hyung-il has outlined comprehensive government measures to stabilize housing conditions and strengthen livelihoods. The administration plans to supply 1.19 million public housing units, with particular emphasis on supporting first-time homebuyers and rental assistance programs. Government officials emphasized that housing policies will focus on stabilizing prices while maintaining affordability for ordinary citizens. The policy framework aims to balance construction approvals, which increased 40 percent this year in Seoul, with market realities that have pushed residents toward increasingly precarious rental situations.

## Jeonse Fraud Relief Legislation

Starting November 13th, victims of jeonse fraud will receive minimum government guarantees covering one-third of their deposit losses. The special relief law, which passed through government cabinet approval, ensures that victims with deposits up to 1.5 billion won can recover maximum support of up to 50 million won. Applicants must submit claims to the Korea Land and Housing Corporation, which will determine eligibility within 90 days. This landmark legislation represents the government's commitment to protecting consumers in a market plagued by landlord insolvency and inadequate protections for vulnerable renters.

## Kospi Faces Pressure Amid Foreign Selling

The Korean stock market experienced significant headwinds this week as foreign investors liquidated positions, causing the Kospi index to break below the 7,000-point threshold. The index closed at 7,003.74, up 0.46 percent, while the Kosdaq fell 1.00 point or 0.11 percent to 893.29. The won-dollar exchange rate weakened by 7.8 won to finish weekly trading at 1,350.6 won, reflecting capital outflows amid global uncertainty. Despite these domestic challenges, international financial conditions remain volatile as markets await crucial monetary policy signals from the United States Federal Reserve.

## Global AI Rally Continues Despite Rate Concerns

The Nasdaq index reached all-time record highs, surging more than 1.00 percent as technology stocks demonstrated remarkable resilience. This strength persisted even as U.S. Treasury yields spiked sharply, indicating investor confidence in artificial intelligence sector fundamentals. Market participants are closely monitoring the September Federal Open Market Committee meeting minutes scheduled for release on October 7th. Weaker-than-expected employment data released last week has temporarily eased concerns about additional Federal Reserve rate increases this month, though future policy remains uncertain as the central bank navigates conflicting economic signals.

## World Bank Upgrades East Asia Growth Forecast

The World Bank recently raised its 2026 growth forecast for East Asia to 4.50 percent, citing robust artificial intelligence-related export performance as a primary driver. However, the institution also warned that rising interest rates across major central banks could dampen the investment enthusiasm that has fueled AI sector expansion. While the World Bank stops short of predicting a complete collapse of AI industry growth, it acknowledges that capital allocation patterns are shifting as funding costs increase and investors reassess valuations across the technology sector.

## IMF Assessment Methodology Creates Disadvantage for Korea

The Bank of Korea expressed concerns that the International Monetary Fund's revised External Balance Assessment model unfairly penalizes South Korea's current account position. The new methodology undervalues Korea's structural advantages, including its semiconductor export boom and demographic dividend factors that support long-term balance of payments strength. This technical reassessment could influence international financial discussions and policy coordination, potentially constraining Korea's negotiating position on exchange rate and macroeconomic policy matters within global institutions.

## Hyundai Motor Group Accelerates Electric Vehicle Production

Hyundai Motor Group's electric vehicle deliveries surged 20.4 percent during the first eight months of 2026, significantly outpacing global industry growth rates. However, Korean battery manufacturers faced competitive pressures, with market share declining 3.9 percentage points year-over-year. Global supply chain competition intensified as Chinese competitors captured market share through aggressive pricing strategies and expanded manufacturing capacity.

## Semiconductor Industry Positioning for Long-term Growth

South Korea's semiconductor sector maintains strategic importance as global artificial intelligence infrastructure demands escalate. Regional development initiatives focus on leveraging Jeolla region's abundant renewable energy resources and surplus power generation capacity, with electricity self-sufficiency reaching 213.4 percent and renewable energy surplus rates at 53.1 percent. This positions southwestern Korea as a secondary semiconductor manufacturing hub capable of supporting energy-intensive chip production operations as global facilities expand to accommodate AI data center requirements.

## Investment Implications for Market Participants

Investors should monitor upcoming corporate earnings releases beginning next week and the Federal Reserve's policy communications this week, which will significantly influence global market direction. Domestic investors should carefully evaluate sector rotation opportunities, particularly between technology stocks benefiting from AI investment trends and value plays in traditional industries. Housing market participants face mixed signals as government intervention increases while rental cost pressures persist, suggesting cautious engagement in residential real estate transactions. The combination of foreign capital outflows, elevated Treasury yields, and Samsung Electronics earnings expectations will likely determine whether Korean equities can establish sustainable support above 7,000 points on the Kospi index.
